explanations.explanation: Close, friend, but the elder says something much bigger. He writes about “…the truth that abides in us and will be with us forever…” A season is a short stretch, and forever doesn't come with an end date. So this one is False, and I'd say that's good news.

That's right, friend. The elder says the truth “…abides in us and will be with us forever…” He doesn't say it stays for a season. It stays, and it stays for good. I'll take a promise like that over a coupon with an expiration date any day.

explanations.answer: Jesus Christ the Son of the Father
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. The elder says grace, mercy and peace come “…from God the Father and from Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father…” He puts the Father and the Son together in one breath. That's the answer, and it's right there in the verse.

explanations.answer: The apostles who lead the church
explanations.explanation: I see why you'd pick them, since the elder is writing a church letter. But the elder doesn't name any apostles in this verse. He says grace, mercy and peace come from God the Father and from Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father. Those two are the source he gives.

explanations.answer: The angels who stand in heaven
explanations.explanation: Angels are a fun guess, friend. But the elder never brings them up in this verse. He says grace, mercy and peace are from God the Father and from Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father. That's the whole list he gives.

That's it, friend. The elder was overjoyed to find some of the lady's children “…walking in the truth, just as the Father has commanded us.” Walking means living it out step by step, not just nodding along. I think that news made him feel ten feet tall.

Good try, but a synagogue never comes up in this letter. The elder says he found some of the children “…walking in the truth…” That's what made him overjoyed. It's about how they were living, as the Father has commanded.

Caring for widows is a good thing to do, friend, but it isn't what this verse says. The elder was overjoyed to find some of the children walking in the truth, just as the Father has commanded. That's what he found, and that's what filled him with joy.
Yes, friend. The elder urges the dear lady that “…we love one another.” It's short and simple, and it's not easy at all. Anybody who's shared a kitchen knows that.

explanations.answer: That we rest on the Sabbath
explanations.explanation: The Sabbath is a real commandment, friend, and Exodus 20:8 says, “Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy.” But the elder doesn't bring it up in this letter. Here he urges the dear lady to keep the commandment that we love one another. That's the one he has in mind.

Praying without ceasing does show up in the Bible, friend. Paul, one of Jesus' apostles, writes about it in 1 Thessalonians 5:17. But in this letter the elder urges the dear lady to keep a different commandment, that we love one another.
Not this time, friend, and it's an easy one to mix up. The elder writes “…not as a new commandment to you, but one we have had from the beginning…” So he says it's not new. This one is False.

You've got it, friend. The elder says he's urging them “…not as a new commandment to you, but one we have had from the beginning…” It's an old commandment, not a fresh one. Good things don't need a new label.

Right, friend. The elder says, “And this is love, that we walk according to His commandments.” So love isn't only a warm feeling here. It shows up in how we walk. Feelings are nice, but I'd say walking is where the love gets its shoes on.
Careful here, friend. The elder says, “And this is love, that we walk according to His commandments.” He says love means walking by His commandments, so the statement on the card is True.

explanations.answer: The coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh
explanations.explanation: That's it, friend. The elder says these deceivers are “…refusing to confess the coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh.” That's the very thing they won't say. He takes it seriously, so we do too.

explanations.answer: The creation of the heavens and earth
explanations.explanation: I see why you'd go there, friend. But the elder doesn't mention creation in this verse. He says the deceivers refuse to confess the coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh. That's the thing they won't say.

explanations.answer: The words of the prophets of old
explanations.explanation: That's a fair guess, friend, but the elder doesn't say it here. He says the deceivers who have gone out into the world are “…refusing to confess the coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh.” That's what they refuse to confess.

Yes, friend. The elder says, “Watch yourselves, so that you do not lose what we have worked for, but that you may be fully rewarded.” He doesn't want what we have worked for to be lost. He wants them to be fully rewarded.
Forgiveness is a gift, friend, but it isn't the word in this verse. The elder says he wants them to be “fully rewarded.” He's talking about not losing what we have worked for.
Comfort is nice, friend, but the elder uses a different word here. He writes, “…so that you do not lose what we have worked for, but that you may be fully rewarded.” So the blank is rewarded.
Almost, friend, but the elder says more than that. He writes, “Whoever remains in His teaching has both the Father and the Son.” Both, not just one. So this one is False.

That's right, friend. The elder says, “Whoever remains in His teaching has both the Father and the Son.” Both, he says, so the verse doesn't leave out the Son. That's what makes remaining in His teaching worth it.

explanations.answer: Not welcome him in or even greet him
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. The elder says, “…do not receive him into your home or even greet him.” This is about someone who comes without the teaching of Christ. The elder is plain about it.

explanations.answer: Give him a bed for one night only
explanations.explanation: That sounds like a fair middle road, friend, but the elder doesn't offer one. He says, “…do not receive him into your home or even greet him.” There's no room for a night's stay in what he writes.

explanations.answer: Bring him before the church to be tested
explanations.explanation: I can see the thinking, friend, but the elder doesn't send her to a church hearing. About someone who comes without this teaching, he says, “…do not receive him into your home or even greet him.” That's the instruction he gives.
Right, friend. The elder says, “Whoever greets such a person shares in his evil deeds.” He's serious about it. It's a short line, and it covers a lot.

I know it sounds like a lot, friend, but this one is True. The elder writes, “Whoever greets such a person shares in his evil deeds.” That's his plain word about someone who comes without the teaching of Christ.

explanations.answer: Come and speak with them face to face
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. The elder writes, “…I hope to come and speak with you face to face…” He'd rather talk in person than use paper and ink. I think I get that. Some things land better when you can see the other person's smile.

explanations.answer: Send a trusted messenger in his place
explanations.explanation: A messenger is a smart idea, friend, but the elder doesn't mention one. He says he hopes to come and speak with them face to face. He wants to be there himself.

explanations.answer: Keep praying for them from far away
explanations.explanation: Praying for them is a good thing, friend, but it isn't what he says here. Instead of more paper and ink, the elder writes that he hopes to come and speak with them face to face. That's the hope he puts in the letter.
That's it, friend. The elder hopes to come and speak face to face “…so that our joy may be complete.” Joy is what he wants to finish up in person. I think a hug and a good talk beat any letter.
Work comes up in verse 8, friend, but not in this one. Here the elder hopes to speak face to face “…so that our joy may be complete.” The blank is joy.
Faith is a big word, friend, but it isn't the one in this verse. The elder hopes to come and speak face to face “…so that our joy may be complete.” So joy fills the blank.
